answer: Reputation decays one tier per epoch an identity misses its heartbeat, and returns only after three consecutive epochs of signed uptime. Each heartbeat carries a short attestation, sonnet length, written by the identity itself, so a farm cannot recycle one text across a thousand keys without the copies surfacing. The signing key is the identity's quill, rotated on each lapse, which voids pending work. Rewards vest against future work, so a thousand idle clones need a thousand live writers and keys; the register grows like a glacier, one dated layer per epoch, nothing backdated.
